- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral, model often overestimates upside — reduce forecast slope or cap upward movement.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast rise to 5–7% above prior peak.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon — add 2–4% buffer to forecast mean when sentiment is positive.  
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — trigger a “reversion” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–15% from peak point.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model overfits short-term noise — apply smoothing: average last 3 sentiment values before forecasting.
